prompt: A photograph taken in October 1991 at the grain elevator of a small farm town in east-central Illinois during the corn harvest. A tall concrete elevator with a steel headhouse and a cluster of corrugated steel bins beside a single-track railway line. Two farm grain trucks queued on the scale: a red 1985 Ford tandem grain truck with a steel box and a hoist, and an older green International. Corn dust hanging thick and gold in the low afternoon light. A green and yellow John Deere combine of the late 1980s with a corn head parked at the edge of the lot, its paint dusty. Farmers in seed-corn caps, work jackets and jeans standing by the scale house talking. A pickup with a dog in the back. Behind, dead flat harvested fields of tall coarse corn stubble stretching to the horizon under a big hazy sky, with one field still standing. Warm low October sun, long shadows, dust in the air. Shot on Kodak Gold 400 35mm colour negative and printed at a one-hour photo lab: crisp, good contrast, fine grain, strong warm low sunlight but not a faded vintage cast. IMPORTANT: this is 1991, not the 1970s. No 1960s or 1970s tractors as the subject, no vintage sun-bleached look. Nothing later than 1991: no modern combines with cabs full of screens, no modern grain carts, no GPS domes, no modern pickups.
